## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6475-gantt-block-face-declared.md`

- names `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx` → `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx` — edited by this change

  > Maintainer ruling, objectui#6475 (2026-08-27), **Option A** — enforce as-is, immediately, no warning window (the startup-stage no-gradualism rule, objectstack#12668: transitions do not get phased windows without named external-user evidence, and none exists here). A census of every `gantt` block reachable through `ObjectGanttSchema` in this repository — the `examples/schema-catalog` fixtures, `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx`, and the published `skills/objectui/guides/page-builder.md` guide — found **zero** blocks missing the trio.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `5b2ea1757` (merge-base with origin/main): 1 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1750 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2354 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36576808603)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1860a3011ffc3cc26fc7874dd8ecf871a247bcd9`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card objectui#10866 (body and all 37 comments, ruling `5890704219` letter A binding, dev report `5891748134`), PR objectui#11110 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the 39 latest check-runs on the head, and `packages/plugin-gantt/src/GanttView.tsx`, `packages/plugin-gantt/README.md` and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx` at the head through the contents API. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The diff is what the ruling ordered — right.** One file, `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx`, +3/-1. The "Drag-and-drop rescheduling" bullet's clause "keeps each date's time of day across a daylight-saving change" gains the parenthetical "(with shift bands configured via `timeSegments`, a day-view drag goes by bands instead, and a move keeps the bar's elapsed length)". No other line moves; no code, no README edit, no changeset. That is exactly the execution parameter of ruling `5890704219`: the mdx's DST sentence gains the shift-band exception matching the README's existing qualifier. Nothing else on the card is touched or judged.
2. **The sentence is true of `GanttView.tsx` at the head — right.** `computeDragChanges` takes its shift-band branch only when `segActive` holds, which is `viewMode === 'day'` and a non-empty `shiftSegments.bands` — so "day-view" is the correct qualifier (a `timeSegments` config under any other scale takes the calendar-day path). In that branch `shift` is `foldShiftRef.current`, which is `shiftByWorkingColumns` whenever `segmenting` holds; it binary-searches `colStartMs` for the column holding the date and returns `colStartMs[target] + offset`. In shift mode the columns are one per band, each `date` advanced by `band.durMs`, so `colStartMs` are band starts and one column step is one band. The pointer handler measures `unitDelta` in `dragColWidth`, the smallest band's pixel width on this scale. So "a day-view drag goes by bands" holds for a move and for both edge resizes: `move` sets `start = shift(originStart, unitDelta)`; `resize-left` shifts the start edge, `resize-right` the end edge, each floored at the smallest band's `durMs`.
3. **"a move keeps the bar's elapsed length" — right, and correctly scoped to a move.** In the same branch `end = originEnd + (start - originStart)` in milliseconds, so the bar's elapsed span is unchanged by a move; `groupMover(..., byElapsedTime)` does the same for a summary's subtree. An edge resize changes the length by whole bands, which is why the mdx attributes the elapsed-length claim to a move only. The dev's deviation 3 (mdx says "a drag goes by bands" and "a move keeps the elapsed length", not the README's "a drag ... keeps") is the accurate reading of the code, not a drift from it.
4. **"instead" versus the calendar-day rule — right.** On the shift-band axis the drag does not snap to whole days and does not keep wall-clock time across a DST change: it moves by elapsed milliseconds along the band columns, which is precisely the behaviour ruling A keeps ("moves by bands on the elapsed-time axis it is drawn on, as today"). Every other scale takes the `calendarDaysBetween` plus `addUnits` path (time of day kept), so the bullet's main clause stays true for them.
5. **Matches the README qualifier's meaning — right.** `packages/plugin-gantt/README.md`, "Drag-and-drop rescheduling": "With shift bands configured (`timeSegments`), a day-view drag moves by bands instead and keeps the bar's elapsed length." Its paragraph's governing sentence is "A move shifts the start and the end by the same number of calendar days ...", so the README's "keeps the bar's elapsed length" is the move's property by context; the mdx says the same thing with the subject made explicit. Same exception, same scale, same two facts; the mdx is the stricter of the two, as the PR body says.
6. **No accept-set or public-surface change — right.** `content/docs` is the docs site, not a package; no prop, type, export, schema or behaviour moves. `snapToBandStart` (the reschedule cascade's snap) is not claimed by the sentence and is unaffected.
7. **Check-runs on the head are the gate verdicts.** 39 latest runs, all `completed`: 36 `success`, 3 `skipped` by design (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard)`), 0 failures. The docs-family runs that this diff can reach — Internal Docs Link Check, Doc Fence Language Check, Doc Component Type Check, Doc Example Id Check, Doc Snippet Type Check, Build Docs, Control Byte Scan, Line Citation Gate, Docs Route Eager Closure Check — are all `success`, as are Changeset Declaration, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check, Lint, Build and E2E and every test shard.
8. **Closing line — right.** Line 1 of the PR body is `Fixes #10866`; the ruling says the card closes `completed` when this docs PR lands, with the closing comment recording the re-entry condition (a real `timeSegments` author in a DST zone leads to letter B as its own card; C never). That closing comment is the seat's act at landing, not part of this diff.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` on the PR body and on the claim `5891317548` — right. The diff publishes nothing: one prose sentence in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx`, outside every package. No changeset is owed for `content/docs`, and none is present; the head's Changeset Declaration and Changeset Claim Re-read runs both `success`, and the dev's `check-changeset-presence` read ("no changeset is owed", 0 published source files) agrees. Confirmed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `5891748134`: `open_questions` is empty; four `deviations` and one `out_of_scope_findings` entry.

- Deviation 1 (the order's `check:doc-links` is not a script; `docs:check-links` was run): answered. The right script was run, and the head's Internal Docs Link Check run is `success`, which is the gate verdict here anyway.
- Deviation 2 (model-free commit trailer per objectui AGENTS.md instead of the harness reminder's trailer): answered, not a contract item. The repo's rule wins on its own repo; no model identifier appears in the PR title or body. Nothing to escalate.
- Deviation 3 (mdx attributes elapsed length to a move, not to any drag): answered in ① items 3 and 5 — the narrower wording is the true one against `computeDragChanges`, and it carries the README qualifier's meaning.
- Deviation 4 (no local build, type-check, package test or eslint): answered. Declared narrowing for a docs-only prose edit outside any package; the head's Type Check, Lint, Build and E2E, Build Docs and all eight test shards are `success`, so nothing the narrowing skipped is unanswered.
- Out-of-scope note (the README's qualifier "a day-view drag ... keeps the bar's elapsed length" sits in a paragraph about moves, so an edge resize on the shift-band scale, which changes the length, is implied only by context): answered, agree with "noted, not filed". The README's paragraph is governed by "A move shifts ..." so its qualifier reads as the move's property; it is not false, only less explicit than the mdx. The order forbade README edits, the ruling records zero `timeSegments` authors in both repositories, and letter B's re-entry rebuilds the shift axis and would rewrite that paragraph with it. Polish, no reach, no carrier owed. Not escalated.

No other flag in the PR body or the dev report; no boundary left open.

Which one is there depends on whether the drill-down query has resolved. It is a race in a pin this seat landed with PR objectui#11099.
